lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: the conditional probability formula as a fraction of outcomes
lessonRef.title: Transfer challenge: the conditional probability formula as a fraction of outcomes

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

items.prompt: P(delay | rain) = P(delay). What does that mean?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A box holds 20 items, of which 7 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.
Given P(A and B) = 16/100 and P(B) = 84/100, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Given P(A) = 12/100, P(B) = 10/100, and P(A and B) = 4/100, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.
In a study, P(passes | attended the workshop) is higher than P(passes) overall. What is the correct interpretation?
choices: The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.
The relationship proves that one event causes the other.
The two events are mutually exclusive.
Attendance and passing are associated, though this alone does not show that the workshop caused the improvement.

items.prompt: A box holds 7 items, of which 3 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: Given P(A and B) = 60/100 and P(B) = 82/100, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Given P(A) = 30/100, P(B) = 38/100, and P(A and B) = 18/100, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: In a study, P(has the condition | tested positive) is much smaller than P(tested positive | has the condition). What is the correct interpretation?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
